螢幕看了七分鐘，游標在輸入框裡閃，一個字都沒打。

他起身去洗那疊放到早上的碗，水聲蓋過一切的時候，身體已經先選好了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合用在資料查完、比較表也做完，卻還是選不下去的那個晚上。
variations: 所有資料都齊了還是決定不了，代表你在等的東西從來不是資料。
比較表可以列到第五年，身體只認得眼前這一秒。

en.content: Twelve forty at night, two offer letters pasted side by side into the chat box, with one line under them: which one should I take. Three seconds later a very tidy table comes back, commute times, salary bands, industry outlook, even the five-year risks. He looks at the screen for seven minutes, cursor blinking in the input field, and types nothing. Then he gets up to wash the dishes he left since morning, and somewhere under the running water his body has already picked.
en.editorNote: For the night when you have collected every piece of information, built the table, and still cannot choose.
variations: When more data stops helping, data was never what you were waiting for.
A table can project five years out; the body only recognizes right now.

items.sourceNote: Manifesting Generator skip-and-return work pattern told as a misread-then-reveal about flat-pack furniture; distinct from the existing entry about MGs moving too fast for the people around them

zh-tw.content:
他把新買的層架整箱拆開，說明書連翻都沒翻，二十分鐘就立起來了。

全家看著地板上多出來的兩顆螺絲，覺得這個人做事真的不能信。

他自己拆掉一層重鎖，把那兩顆補回去，前後加起來還是比隔壁那間快了一小時。

顯示生產者的路線就長這樣，先衝到底再回頭補，那趟折返本來就算在流程裡面。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個老是被念「怎麼都不看說明書」的家人，也適合自己拿來解釋為什麼中途會折返。
variations: 跳過的步驟不會消失，它會排在後面等你回來。
先做完再修，跟先想完再做，最後花掉的時間可能一樣。

en.content: He got the new shelf out of the box, never once opened the instructions, and had it standing in twenty minutes. The whole family stared at the two leftover screws on the floor and decided he could not be trusted with anything. He pulled one tier apart on his own, drove both screws back in, and still finished a full hour ahead of the neighbors. That backtrack is how a Manifesting Generator runs, and the trip back was always on the schedule.
en.editorNote: Send it to the relative who keeps asking why you never read the manual, or keep it for explaining your own habit of doubling back.
variations: A skipped step doesn't disappear; it waits in line behind you.
Build then fix, or think then build, and the clock often lands in the same place.

items.sourceNote: Emotional wave versus in-the-moment authority as a household logistics problem between two people with different authorities; the existing relationship entries cover connection types, not decision lag

zh-tw.content:
「這間我看了很喜歡，房東說今天下訂就幫我們保留。」

「給我三天。」

一個人的答案在當下就到位，另一個要等一整條情緒波走完高低，才分得出來那是真的想要，還是被現場的氣氛推的。

同住的兩個人權威不一樣時，最省事的做法是把那三天先排進行事曆，當成搬家成本的一部分。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合情侶或室友一起看房、買大東西的時候拿出來對照，免得把「等一下」聽成「不想要」。
variations: 決定的速度不一樣，跟認不認真是兩回事。
同居要對的不只作息，還有各自做決定需要的時間。

en.content:
"I really like this one, and the landlord says a deposit today holds it for us."

"Give me three days."

One of them has an answer on the spot, and the other has to ride a whole emotional wave, high and low, before the wanting can be told apart from the mood in the room.

When two people under one roof run on different authorities, the cheapest move is to put those three days on the calendar and count them as part of the moving cost.
en.editorNote: Good for couples or roommates touring apartments and buying big-ticket things, so that a request to wait stops being heard as a no.
variations: Deciding at different speeds says nothing about who cares more.
Living together means syncing more than schedules; decision time counts too.

items.sourceNote: Environment arrow from the Variable system, told as a year-over-year contrast about where the work actually gets done; the arrows have never been used in this topic before

zh-tw.content:
還在前一份工作的那陣子，他在家裡隔出一間書房，買了升降桌、遮光窗簾，還有一把三萬塊的椅子。

今年他每天走十分鐘去巷口那家會放老歌的早餐店，坐同一個角落，用一張會晃的桌子把事情做完。

人類圖把「適合待在什麼樣的地方」畫成圖表下方那幾個小箭頭，有人要安靜可控，有人要一點人聲跟隨機。

那把三萬塊的椅子現在給貓睡，工作卻都是在那張晃來晃去的桌上收尾的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合用在「環境明明很完美卻做不出東西」的困惑上，人類圖的環境箭頭講的正是這件事。
variations: 安靜又可控的房間，對某些人來說反而是最難產出的地方。
換個地方坐一個禮拜，可能比換三套生產力方法有用。

en.content: Back in his last job he walled off a home office and bought a standing desk, blackout curtains, and a nine-hundred-dollar chair. This year he walks ten minutes to the breakfast shop on the corner that plays old songs, takes the same seat, and finishes everything on a table that wobbles. Human Design puts the question of where you work best into those small arrows under the chart, where some bodies want quiet and control and others want a little noise and randomness. The nine-hundred-dollar chair belongs to the cat now, and the work still gets finished on the table that rocks.
en.editorNote: For the puzzle of owning a perfect setup and producing nothing in it, which is exactly what the environment arrow is about.
variations: A quiet, controlled room is the hardest place to produce for some people.
Changing where you sit for a week can beat changing your productivity system three times.

items.sourceNote: Gate 22 grace and the tidal nature of an emotional wave, written as a single wedding-banquet scene; gate 22 has never appeared in this topic

zh-tw.content:
表姊的喜宴把她排在最角落那桌，整晚幫不熟的長輩夾菜、翻譯菜名、笑著聽同一個笑話講三次。

散場前她還留下來把伴手禮一袋一袋分好，每個人都說她好會照顧人。

走到停車場，她上車、扣好安全帶、兩手放在方向盤上，然後就沒有再動了。

人類圖把她那格溫柔畫成有漲有退的潮汐，漲滿的時候撐得住一整場喜宴，退掉之後剩下的力氣，剛好夠她坐在沒開燈的車裡。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種「在場合裡表現得無懈可擊、回到車上卻整個人關機」的朋友，讓他知道那不是雙面人。
variations: 社交能量退潮的時候，連發動車子都要等一下。
撐得住一整場，跟撐得住回家的路，是兩件不同的事。

en.content: Her cousin's wedding banquet put her at the far corner table, where she spent the night refilling teacups for relatives she barely knew and laughing at the same joke three times. She stayed after to sort the favor bags one by one, and everyone told her she was so good with people. Out in the parking lot she got in, buckled up, put both hands on the wheel, and didn't move. Human Design draws that kind of warmth as a tide with a high and a low; at high water it carries a whole banquet, and what's left at low water is exactly enough to sit in an unlit car.
en.editorNote: For the friend who is flawless at the event and completely offline by the time they reach the car. It isn't two-facedness, it's a tide.
variations: When the social tide goes out, even starting the car takes a minute.
Getting through the room and getting through the drive home are two different budgets.

items.sourceNote: 2026 lunar nodes travelling the 37-40 axis, belonging versus self-sufficiency, told entirely through a running count of family dinners

zh-tw.content:
八年來每個禮拜六六點，他都會出現在爸媽家那張圓桌旁邊，出差、感冒、分手都沒有斷過，他算過大概是四百一十七次。

三月的某個星期五，他在家庭群組打了「這週我不過去」，送出以後把手機蓋在桌上。

十一分鐘後媽媽回了一個貼圖，四百一十七這個數字就停在那裡了。

人類圖今年把很多人推到「屬於誰」跟「一個人也行」的兩邊，而他量出來的距離，是十一分鐘。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合用在第一次拒絕家庭固定行程、還在等天塌下來的那個週末。
variations: 拒絕一次不會拆掉八年，這件事要親自試過才會信。
有些界線的代價，實測起來比想像中短很多。

en.content: For eight years he showed up at his parents' round table at six every Saturday, through work trips, flu, and one breakup, and by his own count that came to about four hundred and seventeen dinners. On a Friday in March he typed "not coming this week" into the family chat and laid his phone face down on the table. Eleven minutes later his mom sent back a sticker, and the number stopped at four hundred and seventeen. The nodes this year keep pushing people between belonging to someone and being fine on their own, and the distance he actually measured was eleven minutes.
en.editorNote: For the weekend someone finally skips the standing family thing and is still bracing for the sky to fall.
variations: One no doesn't undo eight years, but you have to test it yourself to believe it.
The price of a boundary usually measures shorter than the fear of it.

items.sourceNote: Root center adrenaline pressure and pacing, delivered as a chain of unexplained cause-and-effect claims rather than an explanation

zh-tw.content:
通勤的 Podcast 從兩倍速調回原速之後，他那個月的睡眠就正常了。

睡眠正常之後，他在會議上講的話少掉三分之二，季末考核拿到進公司以來最好的一次。

考核出來以後，他開始提早二十分鐘出門，走去公司的那一段路上什麼都不聽。

人類圖把那股「快一點、再快一點」放在圖的最底下那格，他沒有去研究那格，他把耳機音量往下轉了一格，這招到現在都還有效。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合送給那種一睜眼就覺得自己落後別人的人，讓他先從一個很小的旋鈕開始。
variations: 把速度調慢一格，有時候比多裝三個效率 App 有用。
急不是個性，是身體最底下那格被踩住了。

en.content: He put his commute podcasts back from double speed to normal, and that month his sleep straightened out. Once he was sleeping, he said about a third as much in meetings, and his quarterly review came back the best one he's had at that company. After the review he started leaving twenty minutes early and walking the last stretch to the office with nothing in his ears. Human Design puts that whole hurry-up-and-hurry-more feeling in the bottom square of the chart; he never went and read about the square, he turned the volume down one notch, and it still works.
en.editorNote: For the person who wakes up already feeling behind everyone else. Start with one very small dial.
variations: Turning the speed down one notch can beat installing three more productivity apps.
The rush isn't a personality trait, it's a pedal at the bottom of the chart being held down.

items.sourceNote: Beginner chart-reading order (type, authority, profile, channels, incarnation cross) used as a list whose final entry is not a chart element at all

zh-tw.content:
他手機備忘錄裡有一頁叫「我的圖」，開頭寫著顯示生產者，接下來是情緒權威、五一人生角色。

再往下是兩條背得出編號、卻說不出功用的通道，還有一個查過三次還是記不住的輪迴交叉名字。

這些他抄了兩個晚上，每一行都很正確，也每一行都用不上。

那頁最後一行是後來才補上去的：上禮拜三下午四點，走出公司大樓，肩膀突然變輕。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給剛排完圖、把名詞抄滿一整頁卻不知道下一步的新手。
variations: 抄得再滿的一頁，抵不過一次身體真的鬆下來的紀錄。
圖上的名詞是索引，能用的部分永遠在生活裡。

en.content: There's a note on his phone called "my chart" that opens with Manifesting Generator, then emotional authority, then 5/1 profile. Below that sit two channels he can recite the numbers of but not the purpose of, plus an incarnation cross he has looked up three times and still can't hold in his head. It took him two evenings to copy all of it down, and every line is accurate and every line is unusable. The last line was added later: Wednesday, four in the afternoon, walking out of the office building, shoulders suddenly light.
en.editorNote: For the beginner who has filled a whole page with chart vocabulary and has no idea what the next step is.
variations: A full page of terminology loses to one logged moment of your body letting go.
The words on the chart are the index; the usable part is always out in your week.

items.sourceNote: Emotional authority — no truth in the now, let the wave finish before deciding; rendered as an inventory of a post office writing counter

zh-tw.content:
郵局那張填單台上有什麼，我三天內數過三遍。
一支綁著棉繩的原子筆，繩子短到要整個人彎腰才寫得到字。
三張寫壞的匯款單，其中兩張是同一個人的筆跡。
一罐蓋子不見的膠水，旁邊躺著壓信封用的鐵尺。
一本翻到起毛邊的郵遞區號簿，停在中部那幾頁。
一個塑膠盒，裡面兩副老花眼鏡，誰要用都可以拿。
還有我包包裡那封掛號信，跟著我在這張桌子前面來回了三趟。
人類圖把這種「今天先不寄」放在情緒權威那一格，我只知道浪還沒退的時候，郵票黏上去也貼不平。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個已經在櫃檯前面繞第三圈、還在決定要不要寄出去的人。
variations: 同一張填單台，第三天才發現老花眼鏡有兩副，信還在包包裡。
郵票黏上去會不會平，身體比腦袋先知道。

en.content:
Things on the writing counter at the post office, counted three times in three days:
A ballpoint pen on a string so short you have to fold yourself in half to use it.
Three ruined remittance slips, two of them in the same handwriting.
A bottle of glue with no cap, next to the metal ruler for flattening envelopes.
A postcode directory worn soft at the corners, sitting open to the middle-of-the-island pages.
A plastic box with two pairs of reading glasses in it, free for anyone.
And the registered letter in my bag, which has now made three trips to this counter.
Human Design files this kind of not-today under emotional authority. All I know is that while the wave is still up, the stamp won't lie flat either.
en.editorNote: For the person circling the counter for a third time, still deciding whether to send it.
variations: Same counter, third day, and the only new discovery is that there are two pairs of glasses in the box.
The letter isn't hard to write. Whether the stamp goes on flat is something the body knows before the head does.

items.sourceNote: Open/undefined spleen center — amplifying other people's fears about health and safety, mistaking borrowed worry for one's own

zh-tw.content:
凌晨一點的藥局，有個男的把手機舉到嘴邊，照著螢幕上的字一條一條念症狀，念到一半停下來補了一句：這些是我媽的。

他把沒被問到的事也一起說了——她昨天走路的樣子、她這幾天沒吃早餐、會不會只是天氣。

藥師把藥盒推過去，他伸手拿了卻沒有走，站在原地又把同一段話說了一次。

人類圖把這種替別人放大的擔心，放在空白的脾中心，而排在他後面的我，手上那盒胃藥是三分鐘前拿的，我的胃並沒有在痛。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種一聽到別人咳嗽，自己先開始查資料的人。
variations: 深夜藥局最常見的畫面：來的人沒病，病的人在家裡睡。
空白脾中心的日常，是把別人的擔心一路揹到收銀台前面。

en.content: One in the morning at the pharmacy, and a guy is holding his phone up to his mouth, reading symptoms off the screen one line at a time, until he stops halfway to add that these are his mother's. Then he offers everything nobody asked about — the way she walked yesterday, the breakfasts she's skipped this week, whether it might just be the weather. The pharmacist slides the box across, he takes it, and he doesn't leave; he stands there and says the whole thing again. Human Design puts that kind of amplified worry-for-someone-else in an undefined spleen, and me, standing behind him, I picked up this stomach medicine three minutes ago, and my stomach doesn't hurt.
en.editorNote: For the person who starts researching the moment somebody else coughs.
variations: The late-night pharmacy regular: the one who shows up is fine, the one who's sick is asleep at home.
An undefined spleen means carrying somebody else's worry all the way to the register.

items.sourceNote: Projector strategy — waiting for recognition and invitation, and the restlessness of waiting without a task

zh-tw.content:
螢幕上叫到七十號，我手裡是九十七，為什麼光是坐著等，我就開始覺得自己該做點什麼？

為什麼手上什麼都沒做，肩膀反而比開會的時候更緊？

為什麼隔壁那位可以整個人靠在椅背上，看起來像坐在自己家的沙發？

叫號機從七十跳到七十一，旁邊那排連在一起的鐵椅有人起身，整條晃了一下，我把號碼牌對折又攤平，人類圖說投射者的能量要等人開口，我今天只等到九十七。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種一閒下來就懷疑自己在浪費時間的朋友。
variations: 號碼牌上的數字沒有動，我的肩膀先動了。
投射者在銀行的三十分鐘：什麼都沒做，累得像做完一整天。

en.content: The screen says seventy and my ticket says ninety-seven, so why does just sitting here make me feel like I should be doing something? Why are my shoulders tighter now, with nothing in my hands, than they are in a meeting? Why can the guy next to me lean all the way back like it's his own couch? The counter flips from seventy to seventy-one, somebody stands up two seats down and the whole bolted-together row of chairs rocks once, I fold my ticket in half and flatten it out again, and Human Design says a Projector's energy is meant to wait for someone to ask — today I'm only waiting for ninety-seven.
en.editorNote: For the friend who starts suspecting they're wasting their life the second they have nothing to do.
variations: The number on the screen hasn't moved. My shoulders moved first.
Thirty minutes in a bank as a Projector: did nothing, came out tired enough for a full shift.

items.sourceNote: Sacral response for Generators / Manifesting Generators — the body says yes or no before the mind does; written as a warning notice for a bubble tea pickup counter

zh-tw.content:
取餐區使用注意事項（我自己那一版）：
一、聽到號碼再往前，你提早三步站到出杯口，後面那五個人會跟著一起擠上來。
二、封膜機在響的時候不要問「我的好了嗎」，那台機器不會因為你問就轉比較快。
三、手已經伸出去、腦袋還沒決定要拿哪一杯的時候，先把手收回來。
四、走之前確認杯身貼紙上的微糖去冰，走到路口才發現是全糖，你不會回頭，你會喝完。
五、如果你是那種身體先答應、事後才想理由的人，這一米寬的檯面會把你的反應速度放大三倍。
六、人類圖把這種「身體先點頭」叫做薦骨回應，這面出杯台是它的縮小版考場。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個總是比自己的號碼早三步站到出杯口的朋友。
variations: 出杯台一米寬，足夠看出一個人有沒有在等自己的身體開口。
手先伸出去了，腦袋還在算今天第幾杯——這一秒就是薦骨在講話。

en.content:
House rules for the bubble tea pickup counter, my edition:
One: step up when your number is called. Standing three steps early pulls the five people behind you forward with you.
Two: don't ask if yours is ready while the sealing machine is running. It does not spin faster because you asked.
Three: if your hand is already out and your head hasn't picked a cup yet, take the hand back.
Four: check the sticker for less-sugar-no-ice before you walk. If you find out at the crosswalk that it's full sugar, you won't go back, you'll drink it.
Five: if you're the type whose body agrees first and invents reasons later, this three-foot counter will triple your reaction speed.
Six: Human Design calls that body-nods-first thing the sacral response, and this pickup counter is a very small exam room for it.
en.editorNote: For the friend who is always standing at the counter three numbers too early.
variations: A three-foot counter is enough to show whether someone waits for their own body to speak.
The hand is already out and the head is still counting today's drinks — that one second is the sacral talking.
